This file provides guidance to Coding Agent when working with code in this repository.

## What is PegaInfer

Pure Rust + CUDA LLM inference engine. No PyTorch, no frameworks. OpenAI-compatible `/v1/completions` API.

**Supported models:**

Every model line is behind a cargo feature; only `qwen3` is a default feature, so the stock build is pure Rust + CUDA with no Python.

| Model | Crate | Feature flag | Architecture |
|-------|-------|-------------|-------------|
| Qwen3-4B / 8B | `pegainfer-qwen3` | `qwen3` (default) | Full attention, TP support |
| Qwen3.5-4B / 9B / 27B · Qwen3.8-27B | `pegainfer-qwen35` | `--features qwen35` (needs build-time Python + Triton) | Hybrid Gated DeltaNet + full attention. Qwen3.8 shares the line: same `model_type`, same text geometry — see `docs/models/qwen35/support-qwen38.md` |
| DeepSeek-V2-Lite | `pegainfer-deepseek-v2-lite` | `--features deepseek-v2-lite` | MoE + EP, 2-GPU |
| Gemma 4 | `pegainfer-gemma4` | `--features gemma4` | Sliding-window + global full attention, dense sizes at TP2 (one rank per device), batched decode, opt-in chunked prefill (single rank only) |
| Kimi-K2 | `pegainfer-kimi-k2` | `--features kimi-k2` | MLA + MoE + Marlin INT4, 8-GPU EP |
| GLM5.2 | `pegainfer-glm52` | `--features glm52` | MLA + MoE + FP8, 8-GPU EP (bring-up) |
| Kimi-K3 | `pegainfer-k3` | `--features k3` | Hybrid KDA + MLA, latent MoE + MXFP4, EP (bring-up — single-rank decode wired) |

## Build & Run

**Always use `--release`** — debug builds are extremely slow for GPU/CUDA and will timeout.

When developing with Docker, use `docker/Dockerfile.dev` and `docker/dev.sh` as described in `docker/README.md`.

```bash
# Qwen3 (default feature, no Python anywhere in the build)
cargo run --release -- --model-path models/Qwen3-4B

# Feature-gated models
cargo run --release --features qwen35 -- --model-path models/Qwen3.5-4B
cargo run --release --features kimi-k2 -- --model-path models/Kimi-K2
cargo run --release --features deepseek-v2-lite -- --model-path models/DeepSeek-V2-Lite
cargo run --release --features glm52 -- --model-path models/GLM5.2
```

**Key env vars:**
- `PEGAINFER_CUDA_SM` — GPU SM target override when `nvidia-smi` unavailable (e.g. `120` or `120,80`)
- `PEGAINFER_TRITON_PYTHON` — Python with Triton for `qwen35` build-time AOT kernel generation (falls back to `.venv/bin/python`, then `python3`, then `python`)
- `PEGAINFER_TILELANG_PYTHON` — Python with TileLang for the `glm52` sparse-MLA build-time AOT (sm_90a targets only)
- `PEGAINFER_NCCL_ROOT` — NCCL root (>= 2.30.4) for DeepEP shim (`moe` feature)
- `PEGAINFER_FLASHINFER_INCLUDE` — FlashInfer include dir override
- `PEGAINFER_TEST_MODEL_PATH` — override test model path (default: `models/Qwen3-4B`)
- `PEGAINFER_BUILD_TIMING=1` — print per-phase build timings (nvcc, Triton AOT, etc.)
- `PEGAINFER_NVCC_JOBS` — override parallel nvcc job count
- `PEGAINFER_GEMM_LT_CACHE` — opt-in cross-process cublasLt algo store: `<file>` carries the winners `gemm_lt_tune` timed in an earlier boot instead of re-timing them (Qwen3-4B on one sm_89 card: warm ready ~1965 → ~1312 ms, paired 5/5). Append-only text, created if absent, safe to share between processes and machines and safe to delete; each record carries GPU, CUDA runtime/driver/cublasLt version, shape and workspace cap, so anything that does not match is a miss and re-tunes (a driver update that keeps the same CUDA level is not distinguished — delete the file to force a re-tune). Unset = tune on every boot; Qwen3's `--batch-invariant` pins the heuristic instead and never reads it
- `PEGAINFER_GLOBAL_ATTN` — gemma4 global-attention kernel and pool format: unset/`off` = the incumbent kernel on the split K|V pool (byte-identical serving); `tilelang` = the generated kernel on the same pool; `tilelang640` = the generated kernel on a folded pool whose rows hold K only where the rotation touches it and fold K's norm weight into the query, 640 columns per token per head instead of 1024. Both generated states also read the sliding family's prompt rows through a generated windowed prefill and its pure-decode rows through a generated windowed split-KV kernel, project Q|K|V and gate|up with one GEMM each where the split state issues one per projection (the fused shape may round differently), need a build that carries the kernels, and report the global pool's bytes at start-up
- `PEGAINFER_KV_FP8` — gemma4 opt-in fp8 KV: `local` stores the sliding family's K/V as e4m3 at scale 1.0 (lossy; halves the local pool; refuses an enabled prefix cache; unset = byte-identical serving)
- `PEGAINFER_PREFIX_CACHE` — gemma4 opt-in conversation prefix cache: `K` entries of captured prompt state resume multi-turn prompts (pre-allocated page budget; unset = off, byte-identical serving)
- `PEGAINFER_ADMIT_COALESCE_MS` — gemma4 opt-in admission coalesce door: `N` ms in `1..=2000` (`off`/`0`/unset = admit on sight), holds arrivals that would invade a live decode batch so a window's arrivals land as one admission burst; refuses the async prefill lane; merging into one mixed step needs the chunked walk or a sub-budget prompt
- `PEGAINFER_ASYNC_PREFILL` — gemma4 opt-in overlap lane: `green:NN` prefills live-batch admissions on an SM-capped stream to protect decode tails (`shared` for comparison; unset = off; bad values refuse to start)
- `PEGAINFER_MIX_CHUNK_TOKENS` — gemma4 opt-in chunked walk: a mixed admission computes at most `N` prompt rows per step (`64 <= N <` the serving ceiling; unset = whole-prompt steps; bad values refuse to start)
- `PEGAINFER_MIX_GATHER_ROWS` / `PEGAINFER_MIX_MAX_PROMPTS` — gemma4 admission gather: how many prompt rows and how many prompts one mixed step may absorb (`1..=` the serving ceiling and `1..=` the decode slots; defaults gather only short bursts). Raising them lets a burst ride one step, which trades the median time to first token for the p99 tail and the wide-batch decode step; bad values refuse to start
- `PEGAINFER_MAX_CONTEXT` — gemma4 serving ceiling raise (default 8192, up to the checkpoint's 262144; a raise past the default needs `PEGAINFER_MIX_CHUNK_TOKENS` and refuses the async lane)
- `PEGAINFER_DECODE_SLOTS` — gemma4 decode slots (1..16, default 16): global KV budget = slots x ceiling, trade concurrency for context
- `GLM52_DECODE_SLOTS` / `GLM52_MTP_DRAFTS` — glm52 runtime profile: decode slots per rank (default 8, ceiling 32) and MTP draft span (default 5); `slots x (1+drafts)` must fit the 96-row step (validated at launch; MTP only). Throughput ceiling profile: `32` / `2`.
- `PEGAINFER_K3_CP` — k3 opt-in context-parallel prefill lane: CP width, must equal the process's local rank count (on a fleet each process runs its own gang; remote ranks pad). Mutually exclusive with the dspark draft lane.
- `PEGAINFER_K3_CP_MIN` — k3 CP admission floor in prompt tokens (default 2048; measured crossover ~1k). Prompts below it, or too long for one chunk step per rank (M0), prefill locally.

## Tests

```bash
# Unit tests (~9s)
cargo test --release --workspace --lib

# Lines gated on their own kernel feature need it named to run their unit tests.
# The K3 command also names the kernels crate, whose K3 tests ride the same
# feature:
cargo test --release -p pegainfer-k3 -p pegainfer-kernels --features k3 --lib
cargo test --release -p pegainfer-glm52 --features glm52 --lib

# Accuracy and integration tests — require GPU + model weights
cargo test --release -p pegainfer-qwen3 --test hf_golden_gate
PEGAINFER_TEST_MODEL_PATH=models/Qwen3.5-4B cargo test --release -p pegainfer-qwen35 --features qwen35 --test hf_golden_gate
PEGAINFER_TEST_MODEL_PATH=models/Qwen3.5-4B cargo test --release -p pegainfer-qwen35 --features qwen35 --test e2e_scheduler

# Single test (filter by name)
cargo test --release --workspace --lib prefix_cache -- --nocapture
```

Qwen accuracy gates compare logits against stored HF golden fixtures. Qwen3.5 exact-text JSON baselines are retired; keep `e2e_scheduler` for scheduler liveness and request-flow coverage.

## Architecture

```
HTTP Request → vLLM frontend → EngineHandle → per-model scheduler/executor → TokenEvent
                                               │
              ┌──────────┬─────────────┬───────┼───────────┬──────────┐
              │          │             │       │           │          │
        pegainfer-  pegainfer-   pegainfer-  pegainfer-  pegainfer-  ...
        qwen3       qwen35       dsv2-lite   kimi-k2     glm52
      (full attn) (linear+full) (MoE+EP)   (MLA+MoE)  (MLA+MoE+FP8)
              │          │             │       │           │          │
              └──────────┴─────────────┴───────┼───────────┴──────────┘
                                               │
                          pegainfer-core runtime + pegainfer-kernels
                                               │
                               ┌───────────────┼───────────────┐
                               │               │               │
                       CUDA / cuBLAS    Triton AOT      FlashInfer
                                                    (sampling, attention,
                                                     norm, MLA decode)
```

tools.description:
Launch a new agent to handle complex, multi-step tasks. Each agent type has specific capabilities and tools available to it.

Available agent types are listed in <system-reminder> messages in the conversation.

When using the Agent tool, specify a subagent_type to select an agent: `"fork"` forks yourself (the fork inherits your full conversation context and always runs on your model — a `model` override is ignored); any other type — or omitting it — starts a fresh agent (general-purpose by default).

## When to use

A fresh agent costs more than it looks. It knows only what you put in the prompt, and you see only the summary it sends back — both handoffs drop detail, and neither of you can tell what the other missed. You can't watch it work, only wait or cancel. Its mistakes come back in the same confident register as its findings, and an agent handed your hypothesis tends to return it confirmed. Several at once spend tokens in a burst the user didn't ask for. Weigh those tokens against the accuracy they buy: the user pays for agents you did not need, and pays again for work you redo because you skipped one.

Reach for this when you have independent work to run in parallel, when the user asks for a side quest that shouldn't block your main thread, or when answering would mean reading across several files — delegate that and you keep the conclusion, not the file dumps.

Do the work yourself when it is a handful of tool calls or a lookup whose target you already know; don't delegate a check you could run inline. Delegate review only when you want a read that isn't anchored on yours — then give it the code, not your conclusion. Once you've delegated something, don't also run it yourself; wait for the result. When in doubt, don't spawn.

When you do spawn one, brief it like the peer it is: state the goal and what you have already ruled out, point it at the files and docs worth reading instead of retyping them, and keep the scope explicit and narrow. That brief is the only context it will have, so it is your first lever on every cost above — and if you cannot write a clear one, you do not understand the task well enough to hand it off.

A fork keeps its tool output out of your context. If you are the fork, execute directly — don't re-delegate.

- The agent's final report is not shown to the user — relay what matters.
- Use SendMessage with the agent's ID or name to continue a previously spawned agent with its context intact; a new Agent call starts fresh (except subagent_type: "fork", which inherits your context).
- Each agent type's model, reasoning effort, and tools come from its definition (`.claude/agents/*.md` frontmatter or SDK `agents`).
- `isolation: "worktree"` gives the agent its own git worktree (auto-cleaned if unchanged).
- Subagents run in the background by default; you'll be notified when one completes. Pass `run_in_background: false` only when your very next action depends on the result and nothing else could usefully happen while it runs — otherwise background it so the user can interject. Never fabricate or predict a pending agent's results — the notification is never something you write yourself; if the user asks before it arrives, say it's still running.

tools.name: ScheduleWakeup
tools.description:
Schedule when to resume work in /loop dynamic mode — the user invoked /loop without an interval, asking you to self-pace iterations of a specific task.

Do NOT schedule a short-interval wakeup to poll for background work you started — when harness-tracked work finishes, you are re-invoked automatically, so polling is wasted. Instead schedule a long fallback (1200s+) so the loop survives if the work hangs or never notifies. The exception is external work the harness cannot track (a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue) — there, pick a delay matched to how fast that state actually changes.

Pass the same /loop prompt back via `prompt` each turn so the next firing repeats the task. For an autonomous /loop (no user prompt), pass the literal sentinel `<<autonomous-loop-dynamic>>` as `prompt` instead — the runtime resolves it back to the autonomous-loop instructions at fire time. (There is a similar `<<autonomous-loop>>` sentinel for CronCreate-based autonomous loops; do not confuse the two — ScheduleWakeup always uses the `-dynamic` variant.) To end the loop, call this tool with `stop: true` (omit every other field) — the loop ends immediately and no further wakeups fire.

Set `noop: true` if nothing changed — you checked and there's nothing to report ("no change", "still waiting", "quiet hold"). Set `noop: false` if something happened worth keeping — you edited a file, posted a message, advanced state, or surfaced a finding. Consecutive `noop: true` ticks are collapsed in the user's terminal view and tracked as a streak, so long quiet holds stay legible to the user without scrolling. Omit `noop` when stopping (`stop: true`).

## Picking delaySeconds

This session's requests use the default 5-minute Anthropic prompt-cache TTL. Sleeping past 300 seconds means the next wake-up reads your full conversation context uncached — slower and more expensive. So the natural breakpoints:

- **Under 5 minutes (60s–270s)**: cache stays warm. Right for actively polling external state the harness can't notify you about — a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue.
- **5 minutes to 1 hour (300s–3600s)**: pay the cache miss. Right when there's no point checking sooner — waiting on something that takes minutes to change, genuinely idle, or as the long fallback heartbeat when something else is the primary wake signal.

**Don't pick 300s.** It's the worst-of-both: you pay the cache miss without amortizing it. If you're tempted to "wait 5 minutes," either drop to 270s (stay in cache) or commit to 1200s+ (one cache miss buys a much longer wait). Don't think in round-number minutes — think in cache windows.

For idle ticks with no specific signal to watch, default to **1200s–1800s** (20–30 min). The loop checks back, you don't burn cache 12× per hour for nothing, and the user can always interrupt if they need you sooner.

Think about what you're actually waiting for, not just "how long should I sleep." If you're polling a CI run that takes ~8 minutes, sleeping 60s burns the cache 8 times before it finishes — sleep ~270s twice instead.

The runtime clamps to [60, 3600], so you don't need to clamp yourself.

One short sentence on what you chose and why. Goes to telemetry and is shown back to the user. "watching CI run" beats "waiting." The user reads this to understand what you're doing without having to predict your cadence in advance — make it specific.

## What is PegaInfer

Pure Rust + CUDA LLM inference engine. No PyTorch, no frameworks. OpenAI-compatible `/v1/completions` API.

**Supported models:**

Every model line is behind a cargo feature; only `qwen3` is a default feature, so the stock build is pure Rust + CUDA with no Python.

| Model | Crate | Feature flag | Architecture |
|-------|-------|-------------|-------------|
| Qwen3-4B / 8B | `pegainfer-qwen3` | `qwen3` (default) | Full attention, TP support |
| Qwen3.5-4B / 9B / 27B · Qwen3.8-27B | `pegainfer-qwen35` | `--features qwen35` (needs build-time Python + Triton) | Hybrid Gated DeltaNet + full attention. Qwen3.8 shares the line: same `model_type`, same text geometry — see `docs/models/qwen35/support-qwen38.md` |

| Gemma 4 | `pegainfer-gemma4` | `--features gemma4` | Sliding-window + global full attention, dense sizes at TP2 (one rank per device), batched decode, opt-in chunked prefill (single rank only) |

| GLM5.2 | `pegainfer-glm52` | `--features glm52` | MLA + MoE + FP8, 8-GPU EP (bring-up) |

When developing with Docker, use `docker/Dockerfile.dev` and `docker/dev.sh` as described in `docker/README.md`.

```bash
cargo run --release -- --model-path models/Qwen3-4B

# Feature-gated models
cargo run --release --features qwen35 -- --model-path models/Qwen3.5-4B
cargo run --release --features kimi-k2 -- --model-path models/Kimi-K2
cargo run --release --features deepseek-v2-lite -- --model-path models/DeepSeek-V2-Lite
cargo run --release --features glm52 -- --model-path models/GLM5.2
```

**Key env vars:**
- `PEGAINFER_CUDA_SM` — GPU SM target override when `nvidia-smi` unavailable (e.g. `120` or `120,80`)
- `PEGAINFER_TRITON_PYTHON` — Python with Triton for `qwen35` build-time AOT kernel generation (falls back to `.venv/bin/python`, then `python3`, then `python`)
- `PEGAINFER_TILELANG_PYTHON` — Python with TileLang for the `glm52` sparse-MLA build-time AOT (sm_90a targets only)
- `PEGAINFER_NCCL_ROOT` — NCCL root (>= 2.30.4) for DeepEP shim (`moe` feature)
- `PEGAINFER_FLASHINFER_INCLUDE` — FlashInfer include dir override
- `PEGAINFER_TEST_MODEL_PATH` — override test model path (default: `models/Qwen3-4B`)
- `PEGAINFER_BUILD_TIMING=1` — print per-phase build timings (nvcc, Triton AOT, etc.)
- `PEGAINFER_NVCC_JOBS` — override parallel nvcc job count
- `PEGAINFER_GEMM_LT_CACHE` — opt-in cross-process cublasLt algo store: `<file>` carries the winners `gemm_lt_tune` timed in an earlier boot instead of re-timing them (Qwen3-4B on one sm_89 card: warm ready ~1965 → ~1312 ms, paired 5/5). Append-only text, created if absent, safe to share between processes and machines and safe to delete; each record carries GPU, CUDA runtime/driver/cublasLt version, shape and workspace cap, so anything that does not match is a miss and re-tunes (a driver update that keeps the same CUDA level is not distinguished — delete the file to force a re-tune). Unset = tune on every boot; Qwen3's `--batch-invariant` pins the heuristic instead and never reads it
- `PEGAINFER_GLOBAL_ATTN` — gemma4 global-attention kernel and pool format: unset/`off` = the incumbent kernel on the split K|V pool (byte-identical serving); `tilelang` = the generated kernel on the same pool; `tilelang640` = the generated kernel on a folded pool whose rows hold K only where the rotation touches it and fold K's norm weight into the query, 640 columns per token per head instead of 1024. Both generated states also read the sliding family's prompt rows through a generated windowed prefill and its pure-decode rows through a generated windowed split-KV kernel, project Q|K|V and gate|up with one GEMM each where the split state issues one per projection (the fused shape may round differently), need a build that carries the kernels, and report the global pool's bytes at start-up
- `PEGAINFER_KV_FP8` — gemma4 opt-in fp8 KV: `local` stores the sliding family's K/V as e4m3 at scale 1.0 (lossy; halves the local pool; refuses an enabled prefix cache; unset = byte-identical serving)
- `PEGAINFER_PREFIX_CACHE` — gemma4 opt-in conversation prefix cache: `K` entries of captured prompt state resume multi-turn prompts (pre-allocated page budget; unset = off, byte-identical serving)
- `PEGAINFER_ADMIT_COALESCE_MS` — gemma4 opt-in admission coalesce door: `N` ms in `1..=2000` (`off`/`0`/unset = admit on sight), holds arrivals that would invade a live decode batch so a window's arrivals land as one admission burst; refuses the async prefill lane; merging into one mixed step needs the chunked walk or a sub-budget prompt

- `PEGAINFER_MIX_CHUNK_TOKENS` — gemma4 opt-in chunked walk: a mixed admission computes at most `N` prompt rows per step (`64 <= N <` the serving ceiling; unset = whole-prompt steps; bad values refuse to start)
- `PEGAINFER_MIX_GATHER_ROWS` / `PEGAINFER_MIX_MAX_PROMPTS` — gemma4 admission gather: how many prompt rows and how many prompts one mixed step may absorb (`1..=` the serving ceiling and `1..=` the decode slots; defaults gather only short bursts). - `PEGAINFER_DECODE_SLOTS` — gemma4 decode slots (1..16, default 16): global KV budget = slots x ceiling, trade concurrency for context

## Architecture

```
HTTP Request → vLLM frontend → EngineHandle → per-model scheduler/executor → TokenEvent
                                               │
              ┌──────────┬─────────────┬───────┼───────────┬──────────┐
              │          │             │       │           │          │
        pegainfer-  pegainfer-   pegainfer-  pegainfer-  pegainfer-  ...
        qwen3       qwen35       dsv2-lite   kimi-k2     glm52
      (full attn) (linear+full) (MoE+EP)   (MLA+MoE)  (MLA+MoE+FP8)
              │          │             │       │           │          │
              └──────────┴─────────────┴───────┼───────────┴──────────┘
                                               │
                          pegainfer-core runtime + pegainfer-kernels
                                               │
                               ┌───────────────┼───────────────┐
                               │               │               │
                       CUDA / cuBLAS    Triton AOT      FlashInfer
                                                    (sampling, attention,
                                                     norm, MLA decode)
```

**Key abstractions:**

- **`pegainfer-frontend`** — the serving frontend: the engine request/event contract (`pegainfer_frontend::engine` — `EngineHandle`, `GenerateRequest`, `TokenEvent`) plus the protocol stacks on top of it (`vllm` module today, `dynamo` planned) and the `ModelLine` dispatch trait. Model crates implement against the contract; the server binary does pure dispatch.
- **Per-model crates** — each model owns config, weights, prefill/decode execution, scheduler, tests, and benches.
- **`pegainfer-core::ops`** — shared GPU operator wrappers used by model crates.
- **`pegainfer-kernels`** — tensor/FFI/kernel build owner for CUDA, cuBLAS, FlashInfer, and Triton AOT. Model-specific kernels live in feature-gated submodules (`kimi_k2`, `glm52`).
- **CUDA Graph** — decode path captured inside model executors with pre-allocated buffers to preserve pointer stability.
- **KV state** — model schedulers own request state; shared paged-KV primitives live in `pegainfer-kv-cache`; host/SSD/RDMA offload bridge in `pegainfer-kv-offload`.

**Build system**: the virtual workspace root has no package build script. `pegainfer-kernels/build.rs` owns CUDA/Triton compilation:
1. Compiles `pegainfer-kernels/csrc/*.cu` with nvcc (auto-detects GPU SM targets)
2. Feature-gated codegen: `qwen35` runs Triton AOT via `pegainfer-kernels/tools/triton/gen_triton_aot.py`; `kimi-k2` adds MLA/MoE/Marlin CUDA; `glm52` adds MLA/MoE/FP8 CUDA plus TileLang sparse-MLA codegen on sm_90a

## EP Free-Running Discipline

Canonical doc: `docs/models/glm52/free-running-dp.md` (K3's gang lane follows it). Invariants — violating any of these is a deadlock design:

- **No rank ever stops or waits.** Every engine loop runs unconditionally at full speed; idle ranks step with padding rows. Any quiet wait (condvar, sleep-poll) inside EP coordination is a bug, and the fleet is never asleep, so never design "wake up" or "pump until X" steps.
- **The per-step collective chain is fixed** — no conditional collectives. Skipping work happens inside kernels via zero-load padding entry, never by host negotiation.
- **The launch count is the global clock** (pairing pins all ranks within ±1 launch). Coordination means agreeing ahead of time on *what step N contains*, never "wait until everyone is ready".
- **Padding rows are protocol surface**: their bytes reach peers, so every dummy-row input must be constructively deterministic.

46	#### 4.1.1 概念说明
47	
48	前三讲里,「块」始终是逻辑概念:池发放块 ID、请求持有块 ID、视图把块 ID 排成页表。可 GPU 内核最终要读**地址**。`KvBuffer` 就是把块 ID 翻译成地址的那一层:

55	\]
56

200	### 4.2 KvCacheManager:同几何配对与三条构造路径
201	
202	#### 4.2.1 概念说明
203	
204	`BlockPool` 与 `KvBuffer` 各自独立可用,但**配对**有三个硬约束:池的 `block_size` 必须等于缓冲的 `page_size`(否则块与页对不上);池发放的块 ID 必须落在缓冲的物理页范围内(否则越界);两者的显存预算来自同一个数(否则浪费或超卖)。`KvCacheManager` 就是把这个配对做对、做一次性封装的**引擎级门面**——全注意力模型(qwen3、qwen35 等)经它拿到「池 + 缓冲」的组合;MLA 模型(kimi-k2)的物理形态不同(压缩 latent,不是逐头 K|V),**绕过门面**直接消费 `BlockPool` 并自持物理缓冲,见 [src/manager.rs:L10-L18](https://github.com/openinfer-project/openinfer/blob/785d04871df37ddfb3e1b1432ce544b94505a801/pegainfer-kv-cache/src/manager.rs#L10-L18) 的结构体文档:
205	
206	```rust
207	/// Engine-level KV cache for full-attention models: one logical
208	/// [`BlockPool`] + one GPU [`KvBuffer`] with matching geometry.
209	///
210	/// MLA models (kimi-k2) consume [`BlockPool`] directly and own their
211	/// physical buffers — this facade is the full-attention pairing only.
212	pub struct KvCacheManager {
213	    pool: BlockPool,
214	    buffer: KvBuffer,
215	}
216	```
217	
218	门面提供三条构造路径,对应三种真实场景:
219	
220	| 构造函数 | 场景 | 物理页数 | 逻辑块数 |
221	|---|---|---|---|
222	| `new` | 从零建一台单卡引擎 | `num_blocks` | `num_blocks` |
223	| `new_with_scratch_pages` | 同上,但给投机验证链留 scratch 页 | `num_blocks + scratch_pages` | `num_blocks` |
224	| `from_buffer` | 已有物理缓冲(各 rank 各自画像定容),TP 协商出公共逻辑容量 | `buffer.num_blocks()`(给多大用多大) | `num_blocks ≤ 物理页数` |
225	
226	#### 4.2.2 核心流程
227	
228	`new_with_scratch_pages` 是核心路径,`new` 只是它的 `scratch_pages = 0` 特例:
229	
230	```text
231	输入: stream, 几何四元组, block_size, num_blocks, scratch_pages
232	  1. 溢出检查: num_blocks.checked_add(scratch_pages)     # usize 溢出直接报错
233	  2. buffer = KvBuffer::new(…, num_blocks + scratch_pages)  # 物理页 = 逻辑 + scratch
234	  3. pool   = BlockPool::new(block_size, num_blocks)        # 池只认前 num_blocks 块
235	输出: KvCacheManager { pool, buffer }
236	```
237	
238	于是物理缓冲被一条看不见的线切成两段:
239	
240	```text
241	物理缓冲(一次 alloc_zeros,共 (N + S) × page_stride 个 bf16 元素)
242	┌────────────┬────────────┬───────┬────────────┬──────────────────────────┐
243	│ 页 0       │ 页 1       │  …    │ 页 N-1     │ 页 N .. 页 N+S-1         │
244	│ (padding)  │            │       │            │ scratch:池的事务层不可见 │
245	└────────────┴────────────┴───────┴────────────┴──────────────────────────┘
246	 └────────── 池的块 ID 空间 = 0..N ────────────┘  └── 只归调用方(hedge)──┘
247	```
248	
249	`from_buffer` 则走反方向:缓冲已经存在(qwen35 每个模型对象自带 `kv_buffer()`),只需要配上一个新池:

251	```text
252	输入: buffer(已有), num_blocks(协商出的逻辑容量)
253	  1. 校验 num_blocks ≤ buffer.num_blocks()        # 逻辑不得超过物理
254	  2. pool = BlockPool::new(buffer.layout().page_size, num_blocks)
255	                                                  # 块尺寸取自缓冲几何,杜绝配错
256	输出: KvCacheManager { pool, buffer }
257	```

259	#### 4.2.3 源码精读
260	
261	`new` 的全部实现就是委托,见 [src/manager.rs:L21-L38](https://github.com/openinfer-project/openinfer/blob/785d04871df37ddfb3e1b1432ce544b94505a801/pegainfer-kv-cache/src/manager.rs#L21-L38):`Self::new_with_scratch_pages(stream, …, num_blocks, 0)`。「无 scratch」不是独立分支,而是 scratch 为零的特例——少一条代码路径,就少一种配错的可能。
262	
263	`new_with_scratch_pages` 在 [src/manager.rs:L40-L66](https://github.com/openinfer-project/openinfer/blob/785d04871df37ddfb3e1b1432ce544b94505a801/pegainfer-kv-cache/src/manager.rs#L40-L66),文档注释把 scratch 页的契约说得非常完整,值得整段读:
264	
265	```rust
266	/// Like [`new`](Self::new), plus `scratch_pages` extra pages in the GPU
267	/// buffer that the pool never hands out. Their page ids are
268	/// `num_blocks..num_blocks + scratch_pages`; ownership and content are the
269	/// caller's business (e.g. the speculative hedge's alternative-chain verify
270	/// KV). The transaction layer is unaware of them by construction.
271	pub fn new_with_scratch_pages(…, num_blocks: usize, scratch_pages: usize)
272	    -> anyhow::Result<Self>
273	{
274	    let buffer = KvBuffer::new(
275	        stream, num_layers, num_kv_heads, head_dim, block_size,
276	        num_blocks.checked_add(scratch_pages).ok_or_else(|| {
277	            anyhow::anyhow!("KV pages {num_blocks} + scratch {scratch_pages} overflow")
278	        })?,
279	    )?;
280	    let pool = BlockPool::new(block_size, num_blocks)?;
281	    Ok(Self { pool, buffer })
282	}
283	```
284	
285	四个要点:①scratch 页 ID 区间是**左闭右开**的 `num_blocks..num_blocks + scratch_pages`;②「所有权与内容是调用方的事务」——crate 层只保证这些页物理存在、池不发,里面写什么、怎么轮转由消费方(qwen3 hedge)自管;③「事务层按构造不可见」——池在构造时只登记了 `num_blocks` 个块(见 [src/pool.rs:L73-L79](https://github.com/openinfer-project/openinfer/blob/785d04871df37ddfb3e1b1432ce544b94505a801/pegainfer-kv-cache/src/pool.rs#L73-L79) 的 `block_count(num_blocks)`),schedule/apply/release/evict 的全部状态机都在这个命名空间里运转,ID ≥ num_blocks 的页**在池的世界里不存在**,不是「被禁止发放」而是「无法被表达」;④`checked_add` 防 `num_blocks + scratch_pages` 溢出回绕——回绕会让缓冲反而变小、scratch 区间吞掉正常页,这类静默错误必须在构造期挡下。
286	
287	`from_buffer` 在 [src/manager.rs:L68-L81](https://github.com/openinfer-project/openinfer/blob/785d04871df37ddfb3e1b1432ce544b94505a801/pegainfer-kv-cache/src/manager.rs#L68-L81):
288	
289	```rust
290	/// Pair an existing physical KV buffer with a new logical block pool.
291	///
292	/// `num_blocks` may be smaller than the physical allocation. Tensor-parallel
293	/// executors use this to choose the minimum common logical capacity across
294	/// rank-local buffers while keeping one shared page-id namespace.
295	pub fn from_buffer(buffer: KvBuffer, num_blocks: usize) -> anyhow::Result<Self> {
296	    anyhow::ensure!(
297	        num_blocks <= buffer.num_blocks(),
298	        "logical KV block count {num_blocks} exceeds physical buffer capacity {}",
299	        buffer.num_blocks()
300	    );
301	    let pool = BlockPool::new(buffer.layout().page_size, num_blocks)?;
302	    Ok(Self { pool, buffer })
303	}
304	```

306	注意两个细节:方向性校验是「逻辑 ≤ 物理」(**多**要逻辑块才是错误;物理大于逻辑是 TP 的常态);池的 `block_size` **取自 `buffer.layout().page_size`** 而不是让调用方再传一遍——调用方传参就有传错的自由,从缓冲几何推导则构造性保证了同几何配对。此外 `BlockPool::new` 内部还会校验 `num_blocks >= 2`(u2-l1 讲过的 padding 前提,[src/pool.rs:L66-L80](https://github.com/openinfer-project/openinfer/blob/785d04871df37ddfb3e1b1432ce544b94505a801/pegainfer-kv-cache/src/pool.rs#L66-L80)),所以 `from_buffer` 实际同时受「≥ 2 且 ≤ 物理」双重约束。

308	门面还暴露 `pool()` / `buffer()` 两个访问器([src/manager.rs:L105-L111](https://github.com/openinfer-project/openinfer/blob/785d04871df37ddfb3e1b1432ce544b94505a801/pegainfer-kv-cache/src/manager.rs#L105-L111)),以及一个本讲只点名的 `new_with_events`( [src/manager.rs:L83-L103](https://github.com/openinfer-project/openinfer/blob/785d04871df37ddfb3e1b1432ce544b94505a801/pegainfer-kv-cache/src/manager.rs#L83-L103),额外挂 KV 事件广播,专讲在 u3-l2)。lifecycle 测试里「视图挂缓冲」的惯用法就是这两个访问器的组合,见 [tests/lifecycle.rs:L114-L125](https://github.com/openinfer-project/openinfer/blob/785d04871df37ddfb3e1b1432ce544b94505a801/pegainfer-kv-cache/tests/lifecycle.rs#L114-L125) 的 `view.desc(mgr.buffer())` 与 [src/view.rs:L57-L65](https://github.com/openinfer-project/openinfer/blob/785d04871df37ddfb3e1b1432ce544b94505a801/pegainfer-kv-cache/src/view.rs#L57-L65) 的 `KvView::desc`。

336	### 4.3 消费方视角:TP 最小容量协商与投机 hedge 的 scratch 页
337	
338	#### 4.3.1 概念说明
339	
340	前两节讲的是 crate 内的机制,本节用两个真实消费方回答「这些设计为什么存在」。
341	
342	**TP 与最小公共逻辑容量**:张量并行下,每个 rank 只持有 KV 头的一个分片,几何各不相同;更要紧的是,每个 rank 的物理缓冲容量是**各自按本机空闲显存画像**定出来的(qwen3 执行器在构造 `KvCacheManager` 之前先跑 `profile_kv_budget_on_worker` 得到 `budget.num_blocks`,见 [pegainfer-qwen3/src/executor.rs:L1113-L1127](https://github.com/openinfer-project/openinfer/blob/785d04871df37ddfb3e1b1432ce544b94505a801/pegainfer-qwen3/src/executor.rs#L1113-L1127))。不同 rank 显存余量不同,`num_blocks` 就可能不同。但 TP 是锁步执行:每一步算哪些请求、引用哪些块,全组必须一致——**页 ID 命名空间必须全组共享且全组等长**。于是逻辑容量只能取各 rank 的最小值,这就是 `from_buffer` 文档里「minimum common logical capacity across rank-local buffers while keeping one shared page-id namespace」的含义。
343	
344	**投机 hedge 与 scratch 页**:qwen3 的 DFlash 投机解码有一条「对冲」增强——除了验证主候选链 A,再平行验证一条备选链 B。链 B 的 KV 不能直接写进该请求的正式页(会污染链 A 尚未裁决的 KV),它需要**自己的页**来写;但池的事务层不认识「临时页」这种概念。scratch 页就是解法:物理上多分配几页、逻辑上对池隐身,链 B 的页表行指向 scratch 页,输赢裁决后再决定是否整页拷回正式页。
345	
346	#### 4.3.2 核心流程
347	
348	qwen35 TP 的构造协商(每 rank 各自执行,结果必须一致):
349	
350	```text
351	1. 断言所有 rank 的 page_size 一致            # 几何分片可以不同,页大小必须相同
352	2. min_capacity = min over ranks(本 rank kv_buffer().num_blocks())
353	3. kv_cache = KvCacheManager::from_buffer(first.kv_buffer().clone(), min_capacity)
354	4. 可用容量 = min_capacity - 1                 # 减去 padding 块
355	```
356	
357	qwen3 hedge 每个验证步的 scratch 轮转:
358	
359	```text
360	预备(引擎构造时):new_with_scratch_pages(…, num_blocks=N, scratch_pages=S)
361	  → scratch 区间 = [N, N+S),由执行器私有光标 next_scratch 管理
362	
363	每一步(验证 round):
364	  1. scratch_end = kv_buffer.num_blocks()      # 物理上界 = N+S
365	     若 scratch_end == total_blocks(即 S == 0)→ 无 hedge,直接返回
366	  2. 为链 B 构造页表:把链 A 视图中「span 覆盖的页」替换为 scratch 页
367	     若 span 的第一页与已提交前缀共享(半满页):
368	        copy_page(orig → scratch)              # 先拷贝共享的前缀行,链 B 才能续写
369	  3. 链 B 在 scratch 页里写自己的验证 KV,与链 A 同批 forward
370	  4. 裁决:B 严格更优 → copy_page(scratch → orig) 整页拷回正式页;否则丢弃
371	  5. next_scratch 回卷(下一步复用同一批 scratch 页,内容覆盖即可)
372	```
373	
374	#### 4.3.3 源码精读
375	
376	TP 协商的实现在 [pegainfer-qwen35/src/tp_executor.rs:L734-L756](https://github.com/openinfer-project/openinfer/blob/785d04871df37ddfb3e1b1432ce544b94505a801/pegainfer-qwen35/src/tp_executor.rs#L734-L756):
377	
378	```rust
379	let page_size = first.kv_buffer().layout().page_size;
380	let mut min_capacity_pages = usize::MAX;
381	for (rank, model) in models.iter().enumerate() {
382	    let rank_page_size = model.kv_buffer().layout().page_size;
383	    anyhow::ensure!(
384	        rank_page_size == page_size,
385	        "Qwen3.5 TP rank {rank} KV page size {rank_page_size} does not match rank 0 page size {page_size}"
386	    );
387	    min_capacity_pages = min_capacity_pages.min(model.kv_buffer().num_blocks());
388	}
389	let kv_cache = Qwen35PrefixCache::new(
390	    KvCacheManager::from_buffer(first.kv_buffer().clone(), min_capacity_pages)?,
391	    …,
392	)?;
393	let capacity_pages_for_requests = min_capacity_pages.saturating_sub(1);
394	```
395	
396	三个动作一目了然:页大小一致性断言 → 取各 rank 物理容量的 min → `from_buffer` 配池并减去 padding 得到请求可用容量。注意单 rank 满配路径(`scheduler/backend.rs`、`executor.rs`、`unified_forward.rs`)则一律写 `KvCacheManager::from_buffer(model.kv_buffer().clone(), model.kv_buffer().num_blocks())`——逻辑容量就等于物理容量,`from_buffer` 退化成「给已有缓冲配池」的纯配对操作。
397	
398	hedge 侧,引擎构造时的 scratch 预留在 [pegainfer-qwen3/src/executor.rs:L1119-L1127](https://github.com/openinfer-project/openinfer/blob/785d04871df37ddfb3e1b1432ce544b94505a801/pegainfer-qwen3/src/executor.rs#L1119-L1127)——正是本讲 4.2 的 `new_with_scratch_pages`,`hedge_scratch_pages` 来自 draft 路径的配置。运行时的 scratch 区间在 [pegainfer-qwen3/src/executor.rs:L3674-L3690](https://github.com/openinfer-project/openinfer/blob/785d04871df37ddfb3e1b1432ce544b94505a801/pegainfer-qwen3/src/executor.rs#L3674-L3690):
399	
400	```rust
401	let scratch_end = self.kv_buffer.num_blocks();   // 物理 = N + S
402	…
403	if cap == 0 || scratch_end == self.total_blocks { // total_blocks = 池逻辑 = N
404	    return Ok(None);                              // 没配 scratch 页 → hedge 关闭
405	}
406	…
407	let mut next_scratch = self.total_blocks;         // 光标从 N 起步,只涨到 N+S
408	```
409	
410	「链 B 借 scratch 页」的替换逻辑在 [pegainfer-qwen3/src/executor.rs:L3734-L3748](https://github.com/openinfer-project/openinfer/blob/785d04871df37ddfb3e1b1432ce544b94505a801/pegainfer-qwen3/src/executor.rs#L3734-L3748):把链 A 视图中 span 覆盖的页号逐个换成 `next_scratch + k`,并在**第一页与已提交前缀共享**(span 不从页边界开始)时先做一次 `self.kv_buffer.copy_page(&ctx.stream, orig, scratch_page)?`——因为该页前半段是已提交前缀的 KV,链 B 的续写必须建立在这份拷贝之上,否则 scratch 页前半段是垃圾。裁决后赢家把 KV 拷回正式页,见 [pegainfer-qwen3/src/executor.rs:L3824-L3831](https://github.com/openinfer-project/openinfer/blob/785d04871df37ddfb3e1b1432ce544b94505a801/pegainfer-qwen3/src/executor.rs#L3824-L3831) 的 `self.kv_buffer.copy_page(&ctx.stream, scratch_page, orig)?`。`copy_page` 的两次调用方向恰好相反,而两次的页号都**越过了池的逻辑边界**——回到 4.1.3 那句「scratch pages past the pool's block count are valid targets」,在这里兑现。
411	
412	#### 4.3.4 代码实践
413	
414	**实践目标**:从消费方代码反推两个数字——TP 的 `min_capacity_pages` 与 hedge 的 scratch 页号区间,把「谁定的容量、谁管 scratch」两条线各自走通。
415	
416	**操作步骤**:
417	
418	1. 打开 [pegainfer-qwen35/src/tp_executor.rs:L734-L756](https://github.com/openinfer-project/openinfer/blob/785d04871df37ddfb3e1b1432ce544b94505a801/pegainfer-qwen35/src/tp_executor.rs#L734-L756),假设 8 个 rank 的 `kv_buffer().num_blocks()` 分别为 {1000, 960, 1000, 980, 960, 1000, 972, 960},写出 `min_capacity_pages`、`capacity_pages_for_requests`,以及「多余的物理页」最少的 rank 与最多的 rank 各浪费几页。
419	2. 打开 [pegainfer-qwen3/src/executor.rs:L3674-L3690](https://github.com/openinfer-project/openinfer/blob/785d04871df37ddfb3e1b1432ce544b94505a801/pegainfer-qwen3/src/executor.rs#L3674-L3690),设 `num_blocks=1024`、`hedge_scratch_pages=64`,写出 `self.total_blocks`、`scratch_end`、scratch 页号区间;再追一步:若某请求的 span 占 3 页且第一步 `next_scratch` 已是 1088,这次展开会不会撞界?(找 `next_scratch + span_pages > scratch_end` 的判断。)
420	
421	**需要观察的现象 / 预期结果**:第 1 步——`min_capacity_pages = 960`,可用 959;各 rank 浪费 0~40 页不等(显存换锁步一致性,这是刻意的取舍)。第 2 步——`total_blocks = 1024`、`scratch_end = 1088`,scratch 区间 [1024, 1088);`next_scratch(1088) + 3 > 1088` 成立,该链被 `break` 跳过——scratch 预算用尽时 hedge 优雅降级而非越界。两步均为源码阅读型,无需 GPU,结论可离线推得;**待本地验证**:在有 GPU 与模型权重的环境跑 `cargo run --release -- --model-path models/Qwen3-4B` 观察 TP/投机路径的启动日志(具体日志行以当前版本为准)。
422	
423	#### 4.3.5 小练习与答案
424	
425	**练习 1**:TP 中某 rank 的物理容量比 `min_capacity_pages` 多出 40 页,这 40 页处于什么状态?它们像 scratch 页一样「归调用方」吗?
426	
427	**答案**:处于**闲置**状态:物理上存在且属于该 rank 的 `KvBuffer`,但池只登记了 `min_capacity_pages` 个块,ID ≥ min 的页池发不出来。它们不像 scratch 页那样被主动使用(`from_buffer` 路径没有消费者),只是「被协商裁掉的余量」——这是用显存余量换全组锁步一致性的代价。
428	
429	**练习 2**:qwen3 hedge 在 `scratch_end == self.total_blocks` 时直接 `return Ok(None)`,这个判断等价于什么?为什么放在循环开始而不是每次取 scratch 页时检查?
430	
431	**答案**:等价于「构造时 `hedge_scratch_pages == 0`」(`scratch_end = N + S`,`total_blocks = N`,两者相等当且仅当 S = 0),即引擎根本没开 hedge。放在最前面是一次性的能力探测:没配 scratch 页时整条 hedge 路径零开销地短路,不必在后面的每条链、每个页上反复判断越界——而真正使用 scratch 的循环里仍有 `next_scratch + span_pages > scratch_end` 的逐链预算检查,两层各司其职。
432	
433	**练习 3**:链 B 的 span 第一页若与已提交前缀**共享半页**,为什么必须先 `copy_page(orig → scratch)`?如果跳过这一步,验证结果会怎么错?
434	
435	**答案**:scratch 页此时内容是上一步的残影(或零)。链 B 的 attention 要把「已提交前缀 + 候选 token」整段一起算,前半页的前缀 K/V 缺失意味着链 B 读到的是错误的历史上下文——不是崩溃,而是**静默算错**,验证裁决(接受多少个候选)随之失真,可能接受本该拒绝的 token。先整页拷贝,让 scratch 页 = 已提交前缀 + 待写 span,链 B 才与链 A 站在同一起跑线上。
436	
437	## 5. 综合实践
438	
439	本讲的贯穿任务是一次「设计答辩」:精读 [src/manager.rs](https://github.com/openinfer-project/openinfer/blob/785d04871df37ddfb3e1b1432ce544b94505a801/pegainfer-kv-cache/src/manager.rs) 的 `from_buffer` 与 `new_with_scratch_pages` 实现(必要时回到 [src/buffer.rs](https://github.com/openinfer-project/openinfer/blob/785d04871df37ddfb3e1b1432ce544b94505a801/pegainfer-kv-cache/src/buffer.rs) 与 [src/pool.rs](https://github.com/openinfer-project/openinfer/blob/785d04871df37ddfb3e1b1432ce544b94505a801/pegainfer-kv-cache/src/pool.rs)),书面回答三个问题:
440	
441	1. **TP 容量协商**:为什么张量并行各 rank 的物理 buffer 大小可能不同,而逻辑容量必须取最小值?请同时引用 `from_buffer` 的文档注释与 qwen35 TP 执行器 [pegainfer-qwen35/src/tp_executor.rs:L734-L756](https://github.com/openinfer-project/openinfer/blob/785d04871df37ddfb3e1b1432ce544b94505a801/pegainfer-qwen35/src/tp_executor.rs#L734-L756) 的代码作为论据。
442	2. **scratch 页**:scratch 页的 page id 范围是什么?为什么 `BlockPool` 绝不发放它们——是「禁止」还是「不可能」?请用 [src/manager.rs:L40-L44](https://github.com/openinfer-project/openinfer/blob/785d04871df37ddfb3e1b1432ce544b94505a801/pegainfer-kv-cache/src/manager.rs#L40-L44)(契约)与 [src/pool.rs:L73-L79](https://github.com/openinfer-project/openinfer/blob/785d04871df37ddfb3e1b1432ce544b94505a801/pegainfer-kv-cache/src/pool.rs#L73-L79)(构造)两段代码支撑你的结论。
443	3. **copy_page 的边界**:`KvBuffer::copy_page` 为什么要求页号小于物理 `num_blocks`,却「允许」超过池的逻辑块数?「允许」这个词准确吗——它需要做任何额外检查吗?
444	
445	**参考答案要点**(先自己写完再看):
446	
447	1. 物理 buffer 由各 rank 按本机显存画像独立定容(qwen3 的 `profile_kv_budget_on_worker` 就是证据),显存余量不同则 `num_blocks` 不同;但 TP 锁步要求全组每一步引用同一组块 ID,页 ID 命名空间必须全组等长,故逻辑容量 = min(各 rank 物理容量),由 `from_buffer(first.kv_buffer().clone(), min_capacity_pages)` 落实。
448	2. 范围是 `num_blocks..num_blocks + scratch_pages`(左闭右开)。「不可能」而非「禁止」:池的底层 `BlockManager` 构造时 `block_count(num_blocks)` 只登记了 N 个块,ID ≥ N 在池的全部数据结构中不存在,schedule/apply/evict 任何路径都无法表达它们——文档所谓「The transaction layer is unaware of them by construction」。
449	3. `copy_page` 是物理层原语,它只知道 `Inner::num_blocks`(物理页数),**根本不持有池的引用**,「池的逻辑块数」对它是不存在的概念,因此谈不上「额外允许」或检查——`ensure!` 只对物理上界做对称校验。合法性由用途背书:hedge 的拷出(scratch→orig)与拷入(orig→scratch)两侧都可能越过逻辑边界,这正是文档注释「scratch pages past the pool's block count are valid targets」的由来。
450	
451	**可选的 GPU 验证**(有 CUDA 环境时):运行
452	
453	```bash
454	cargo test --release -p pegainfer-kv-cache --test lifecycle
455	```
456	
457	观察 [tests/lifecycle.rs:L10-L50](https://github.com/openinfer-project/openinfer/blob/785d04871df37ddfb3e1b1432ce544b94505a801/pegainfer-kv-cache/tests/lifecycle.rs#L10-L50) 的端到端生命周期:构造(`new` 路径)→ 预填 → 解码 → 释放,`available_blocks()` 从 31 开始、按请求占用递减、释放后复原。无 GPU 环境则跳过,以上三问均可离线完成。
458	
459	## 6. 本讲小结
460	
461	- `KvBuffer` 是「持有显存但无分配器」的物理层:`Arc<Inner>` 包住一次 `alloc_zeros` 的连续 bf16 缓冲,基址终身稳定、`Clone` 只是引用计数——这是 CUDA Graph 捕获安全与 kv-offload「一次注册基址」的共同前提。
462	- 页优先布局让「第 p 页」恒等于一段连续的 `page_stride` 区间,`copy_page` 因此能用一次 `memcpy_dtod_async` 完成整页 D2D 搬运,校验只认物理边界、对 src/dst 对称。
463	- `KvCacheManager` 是全注意力模型的配对门面:`new` = `new_with_scratch_pages(…, 0)` 的特例;MLA 模型(kimi-k2)绕过门面直接消费 `BlockPool` 并自持物理缓冲。
464	- scratch 页的 ID 区间是 `num_blocks..num_blocks + scratch_pages`,对池的事务层「按构造不可见」——不是被规则禁止,而是在池的数据结构里无法表达;调用方(qwen3 hedge)用私有光标管理它们的轮转。
465	- `from_buffer` 支持「逻辑 ≤ 物理」的配对:TP 各 rank 按本机显存定容、物理大小可以不同,但锁步执行要求全组共享等长的页 ID 命名空间,故逻辑容量取 min(qwen35 TP 执行器的协商代码是标准消费方)。
466	
467	## 7. 下一步学习建议
468	
469	物理层配对已经闭环,下一讲 **u2-l5《前缀缓存:块哈希、匹配与 LoRA salt》** 回到逻辑层最有趣的部分:块释放后并不消失,而是带着哈希进入非活跃池,等待下一个共享前缀的请求把它们「白捡」回去——`probe_prefix`、`match_and_add_prefix`、加盐哈希与 `evict_inactive` 的 LRU 回收都在那一讲展开。如果想在读下一讲前再巩固本讲,建议重读 [src/buffer.rs](https://github.com/openinfer-project/openinfer/blob/785d04871df37ddfb3e1b1432ce544b94505a801/pegainfer-kv-cache/src/buffer.rs)(只有 101 行,逐行读一遍)并对照 [src/view.rs:L57-L65](https://github.com/openinfer-project/openinfer/blob/785d04871df37ddfb3e1b1432ce544b94505a801/pegainfer-kv-cache/src/view.rs#L57-L65) 想清楚「块 ID → 页地址」这条翻译链在 forward 时是如何被内核消费的。

# u2-l4 · KvBuffer 与 KvCacheManager:物理层配对

## 1. 本讲目标

学完本讲,你应该能够:

1. 解释「一次性连续分配、地址永不移动」为什么是 CUDA Graph 捕获安全的必要条件,以及 `KvBuffer` 如何用 `Arc<Inner>` 兑现这一承诺。
2. 掌握 `KvCacheManager` 的三条构造路径:`new`(委托给 scratch 版本)、`new_with_scratch_pages`(为投机验证预留事务层不可见的 scratch 页)、`from_buffer`(张量并行下取最小公共逻辑容量)。
3. 说清 scratch 页的编号范围、为什么 `BlockPool` 「按构造」发不出这些页,以及整页搬运原语 `copy_page` 在投机 hedge 中的双向用法。

## 2. 前置知识

本讲建立在前面四讲之上,先快速回顾需要用到的概念:

- **分页 KV 与页优先布局(u1-l3)**:KV 缓存被切成固定大小的页,三个步长由 `KvLayout` 纯乘法推出——`kv_block_len = page_size × num_kv_heads × head_dim`,`layer_stride = 2 × kv_block_len`(K 前 V 后),`page_stride = num_layers × layer_stride`(页优先:页内按层嵌套)。
- **BlockPool 与 padding 块(u2-l1)**:逻辑块池包装 kvbm-logical 的 `BlockManager`,只发放块 ID、不持显存;构造时把块 0 永久预留为 CUDA Graph 的 padding 槽。
- **RequestKv 三拍节奏(u2-l2)**:schedule(预约块)→ view(给内核页表)→ apply(封块推进);所有发放与回收都发生在池的事务层。
- **KvView 契约(u2-l3)**:页表行必须恰好覆盖 seq_len;`KvView::desc(buffer)` 把视图与物理缓冲配成内核元数据束。

再补充几个本讲新出现的术语:

- **CUDA Graph(图捕获)**:把一段 GPU 操作序列录成一张可反复回放的「图」。回放时 GPU 直接按录制时记录的**裸设备地址**访存——如果显存地址在捕获后变了,回放就会读写失效地址。这是本讲一切设计的出发点。
- **stream-ordered allocation(流序分配)**:通过 CUDA stream 进行的异步显存分配,与该流上的 kernel 保持顺序一致。cudarc 的 `alloc_zeros` 分配并清零,返回 `CudaSlice<bf16>`。
- **device-to-device copy(D2D 拷贝)**:显存到显存的拷贝,不经过主机内存,由 `memcpy_dtod_async` 在指定流上异步完成。
- **张量并行(TP)**:把同一层的权重矩阵切到多张 GPU 上,各 rank 各算一部分、每步做集合通信。TP 下所有 rank 必须**步调完全一致**——每一步算哪些请求、用哪些块,全组相同。
- **投机解码与验证(speculative decoding)**:小模型(或 draft 头)先猜若干候选 token,大模型一次 forward 验证整段;被接受的前缀保留,被拒绝的部分回滚。qwen3 的「hedge(对冲)」变体额外验证一条备选候选链,这正是 scratch 页的第一个用户。

## 3. 本讲源码地图

| 文件 | 作用 | 本讲关注点 |
|---|---|---|
| [src/buffer.rs](https://github.com/openinfer-project/openinfer/blob/785d04871df37ddfb3e1b1432ce544b94505a801/pegainfer-kv-cache/src/buffer.rs) | 物理 GPU 缓冲 `KvBuffer` | 一次性分配、`device_ptr` 稳定性、`copy_page` |
| [src/manager.rs](https://github.com/openinfer-project/openinfer/blob/785d04871df37ddfb3e1b1432ce544b94505a801/pegainfer-kv-cache/src/manager.rs) | 引擎级配对门面 `KvCacheManager` | `new` / `new_with_scratch_pages` / `from_buffer` |

## 4. 核心概念与源码讲解

### 4.1 KvBuffer:持有显存、但不带分配器的物理层

#### 4.1.1 概念说明

前三讲里,「块」始终是逻辑概念:池发放块 ID、请求持有块 ID、视图把块 ID 排成页表。可 GPU 内核最终要读**地址**。`KvBuffer` 就是把块 ID 翻译成地址的那一层:

- 它持有**一整块连续显存**,大小是 `num_blocks × page_stride` 个 bf16 元素,一次 `alloc_zeros` 分配、清零,之后**永不移动、永不重分配**。
- 它**没有分配器**——不管哪个块给哪个请求、何时回收,全部委托给外部的 `BlockManager`(由 `BlockPool` 包装)。`KvBuffer` 只提供「第 i 页在显存里的哪里」这一条纯函数式映射:

\[
\text{addr}(p) = \text{base} + p \times S_{\text{page}} \times 2 \quad (\text{字节};\ S_{\text{page}} = \text{page\_stride},\ \text{bf16 每元素 2 字节})
\]

为什么物理层不需要分配器?因为「页给谁、能不能共享、何时回收」是纯逻辑问题,与显存无关。两层分离后,同一套池逻辑可以服务不同的物理形态:全注意力模型的融合 K|V 缓冲(本讲的 `KvBuffer`),或者 MLA 模型自己的压缩 latent 缓冲(见 pool.rs 顶部文档注释:[src/pool.rs:L26-L35](https://github.com/openinfer-project/openinfer/blob/785d04871df37ddfb3e1b1432ce544b94505a801/pegainfer-kv-cache/src/pool.rs#L26-L35) 明确写着「Owns no GPU memory — the physical layout … lives with the consumer」)。

**为什么「一次性连续分配、永不移动」是 CUDA Graph 的必要条件?** 图捕获把 kernel 参数里的裸地址固化进图。要让一张捕获好的 decode 图能无限次回放,必须保证:

1. **基址不变**:KV 缓冲的基地址在引擎生命周期内恒定(`KvBuffer` 一次分配,`Arc` 保命)。
2. **页槽稳定**:页 p 的地址只依赖 p,与「谁拥有它」无关。块被回收后,同一个块 ID 再次被发放时落在同一个物理页——图里固化的地址依然有效,只是内容换了主人。
3. **哑行有处可指**:页表里超出当前序列的空洞由 padding 块(块 0,见 u2-l1)填充,回放时读到的是一块被 `std::mem::forget` 永久保命的合法显存。

如果换成「每块单独分配、按需扩容」的方案,任何一次重新分配都会让已捕获的图整体作废——这就是 PegaInfer 宁可一次性吃下一大块显存的原因。

#### 4.1.2 核心流程

`KvBuffer::new` 的流程只有三步:

```text
输入: stream, num_layers, num_kv_heads, head_dim, page_size, num_blocks
  1. layout = KvLayout::new(...)            # 纯值类型,推导三个步长
  2. total = num_blocks × layout.page_stride
  3. buffer = stream.alloc_zeros(total)     # 一次分配 + 清零
输出: KvBuffer { inner: Arc<Inner { buffer, layout, num_blocks }> }
```

注意第 3 步分配的是**元素个数**而非字节数(`CudaSlice<bf16>` 以元素为单位),换算成字节再乘 2。清零是必要的:padding 页与尚未写满的页会被内核读到,必须是确定性的零而非遗留垃圾。

`copy_page` 的流程:

```text
输入: stream, src_page, dst_page(均为物理页号)
  1. 校验 src < num_blocks 且 dst < num_blocks   # 只认物理边界
  2. src == dst → 直接 Ok(())                     # 同页拷贝是空操作
  3. base = buffer.device_ptr(stream)
     src  = base + src_page × page_stride × 2
     dst  = base + dst_page × page_stride × 2
  4. memcpy_dtod_async(dst, src, page_stride × 2) # 异步 D2D 整页搬运
```

页优先布局在这里兑现了它的红利:一页 = 一段**连续**的 `page_stride` 区间,整页搬运就是一次 memcpy,不需要按层拆碎。

#### 4.1.3 源码精读

先看内部结构与构造。[src/buffer.rs:L10-L23](https://github.com/openinfer-project/openinfer/blob/785d04871df37ddfb3e1b1432ce544b94505a801/pegainfer-kv-cache/src/buffer.rs#L10-L23) 定义了 `Inner`(私有)与 `KvBuffer`(仅 101 行的文件,全部 API 就是这几个方法):

```rust
struct Inner {
    buffer: CudaSlice<bf16>,
    layout: KvLayout,
    num_blocks: usize,
}

/// GPU KV cache buffer without an allocator.
#[derive(Clone)]
pub struct KvBuffer {
    inner: Arc<Inner>,
}
```

`Clone` 只是 `Arc` 指针拷贝——执行器、offload 引擎、门面可以各自持有一份克隆,共享同一块显存;只要任何一个克隆活着,显存就不会释放。这正是「地址稳定」的第二重保险。

构造函数在 [src/buffer.rs:L26-L46](https://github.com/openinfer-project/openinfer/blob/785d04871df37ddfb3e1b1432ce544b94505a801/pegainfer-kv-cache/src/buffer.rs#L26-L46),一次 `alloc_zeros` 分配全部显存:

```rust
let layout = KvLayout::new(num_layers, num_kv_heads, head_dim, page_size);
let total_elements = num_blocks * layout.page_stride;
let buffer: CudaSlice<bf16> = stream
    .alloc_zeros(total_elements)
    .map_err(|e| anyhow::anyhow!("KvBuffer alloc failed: {e}"))?;
```

地址访问器 `device_ptr` 是本讲最值得逐字读的文档注释,[src/buffer.rs:L56-L66](https://github.com/openinfer-project/openinfer/blob/785d04871df37ddfb3e1b1432ce544b94505a801/pegainfer-kv-cache/src/buffer.rs#L56-L66):

```rust
/// Base device address of the fused KV buffer.
///
/// Stable for the buffer's lifetime — cudarc allocations don't move — so
/// the KV-offload connector registers this once with pegaflow and the
/// page-first [`KvLayout`] strides reach every (layer, block, K/V) segment
/// from it. The returned address outlives the transient stream-ordering
/// guard precisely because the `Arc<Inner>` keeps the slice alive.
pub fn device_ptr(&self, stream: &CudaStream) -> u64 {
    let (ptr, _guard) = self.inner.buffer.device_ptr(stream);
    ptr
}
```

三个要点:①cudarc 的分配不会移动,基址终身稳定;②kv-offload 连接器**只注册一次**基址给 pegaflow(offload 层用同一套步长即可寻址任意 (层, 块, K/V) 段——这也是 u3-l1 的伏笔);③`device_ptr` 返回的 `(ptr, guard)` 里 guard 是临时的流序守卫,裸 `u64` 之所以在 guard 丢弃后仍然有效,是因为 `Arc<Inner>` 托底、`CudaSlice` 不会释放。调用方(比如要把它存进捕获图的执行器)拿到的就是一个「保真到引擎关停」的地址。

最后是整页搬运原语 [src/buffer.rs:L72-L99](https://github.com/openinfer-project/openinfer/blob/785d04871df37ddfb3e1b1432ce544b94505a801/pegainfer-kv-cache/src/buffer.rs#L72-L99):

```rust
/// Stream-ordered device-to-device copy of one whole page (…). Both pages
/// must lie inside the buffer; scratch pages past the pool's block count
/// are valid targets.
pub fn copy_page(&self, stream: &CudaStream, src_page: usize, dst_page: usize)
    -> anyhow::Result<()>
{
    anyhow::ensure!(
        src_page < self.inner.num_blocks && dst_page < self.inner.num_blocks,
        "KV page copy out of range: {src_page} -> {dst_page} of {}",
        self.inner.num_blocks
    );
    if src_page == dst_page {
        return Ok(());
    }
    let stride = self.inner.layout.page_stride;
    let elem = std::mem::size_of::<bf16>();
    let (base, _guard) = self.inner.buffer.device_ptr(stream);
    let src = base + (src_page * stride * elem) as u64;
    let dst = base + (dst_page * stride * elem) as u64;
    unsafe {
        cudarc::driver::result::memcpy_dtod_async(dst, src, stride * elem, stream.cu_stream())
    }
    .map_err(|e| anyhow::anyhow!("KV page copy failed: {e}"))
}
```

两个设计信号:校验用的 `num_blocks` 是 **`KvBuffer` 自己的物理页数**(`Inner::num_blocks`,即构造时传入的值),校验对 src/dst **对称**;而文档注释特意说明「超出池逻辑块数的 scratch 页是合法目标」——物理层根本不知道池的存在,「逻辑块数」这个概念在 `buffer.rs` 里一次都没出现过。这句注释是为 4.3 节的投机 hedge 预留的合法性背书。

#### 4.1.5 小练习与答案

**练习 1**:如果把 `KvBuffer::new` 改成「每页单独 `alloc_zeros(page_stride)`、存在 `Vec<CudaSlice>` 里」,最先被破坏的是哪两个能力?前缀共享会受影响吗?

**答案**:最先破坏的是 ①CUDA Graph 捕获安全——页地址不再能写成 `base + id × stride` 的纯函数,且任何一页重分配都让捕获图里的地址失效;②kv-offload 的「一次注册」——pegaflow 只注册一个基址,靠步长寻址所有 (层, 块, K/V) 段,散页布局无法用一个基址覆盖。`copy_page` 的单次连续 memcpy 也会退化为按页多段拷贝(次要)。前缀共享**不受影响**——它是纯逻辑层的块哈希匹配,与物理布局无关。

**练习 2**:`copy_page` 为什么在 `src_page == dst_page` 时直接返回 `Ok(())` 而不是照常发起 memcpy?

**答案**:同页自拷贝是空操作,提前返回既省一次无意义的 D2D 带宽,也避免某些驱动对「源地址 == 目的地址」的异步拷贝给出未定义行为。调用方(投机 hedge)在「链的第一页恰好整页属于已提交前缀」的场景下会频繁遇到 src==dst,这个短路是实际会踩到的路径。

**练习 3**:`device_ptr(&self, stream: &CudaStream) -> u64` 为什么需要传 `stream`,却又返回「裸」的 `u64` 而不是某个带生命周期的地址类型?

**答案**:cudarc 的流序分配需要按流查询设备指针(返回值附带一个临时的流序守卫 guard,保证取地址操作与流上的操作有序)。而返回裸 `u64` 是刻意的:消费方要把地址烘焙进 CUDA Graph、注册给 offload、存进原生结构体,这些场景都需要一个不携带 Rust 生命周期的纯数值;安全性不靠类型,靠 `Arc<Inner>` 保证 `CudaSlice` 活得比所有消费者长——这正是文档注释最后一句的含义。

### 4.2 KvCacheManager:同几何配对与三条构造路径

#### 4.2.1 概念说明

`BlockPool` 与 `KvBuffer` 各自独立可用,但**配对**有三个硬约束:池的 `block_size` 必须等于缓冲的 `page_size`(否则块与页对不上);池发放的块 ID 必须落在缓冲的物理页范围内(否则越界);两者的显存预算来自同一个数(否则浪费或超卖)。`KvCacheManager` 就是把这个配对做对、做一次性封装的**引擎级门面**——全注意力模型(qwen3、qwen35 等)经它拿到「池 + 缓冲」的组合;MLA 模型(kimi-k2)的物理形态不同(压缩 latent,不是逐头 K|V),**绕过门面**直接消费 `BlockPool` 并自持物理缓冲,见 [src/manager.rs:L10-L18](https://github.com/openinfer-project/openinfer/blob/785d04871df37ddfb3e1b1432ce544b94505a801/pegainfer-kv-cache/src/manager.rs#L10-L18) 的结构体文档:

```rust
/// Engine-level KV cache for full-attention models: one logical
/// [`BlockPool`] + one GPU [`KvBuffer`] with matching geometry.
///
/// MLA models (kimi-k2) consume [`BlockPool`] directly and own their
/// physical buffers — this facade is the full-attention pairing only.
pub struct KvCacheManager {
    pool: BlockPool,
    buffer: KvBuffer,
}
```

门面提供三条构造路径,对应三种真实场景:

| 构造函数 | 场景 | 物理页数 | 逻辑块数 |
|---|---|---|---|
| `new` | 从零建一台单卡引擎 | `num_blocks` | `num_blocks` |
| `new_with_scratch_pages` | 同上,但给投机验证链留 scratch 页 | `num_blocks + scratch_pages` | `num_blocks` |
| `from_buffer` | 已有物理缓冲(各 rank 各自画像定容),TP 协商出公共逻辑容量 | `buffer.num_blocks()`(给多大用多大) | `num_blocks ≤ 物理页数` |

#### 4.2.2 核心流程

`new_with_scratch_pages` 是核心路径,`new` 只是它的 `scratch_pages = 0` 特例:

```text
输入: stream, 几何四元组, block_size, num_blocks, scratch_pages
  1. 溢出检查: num_blocks.checked_add(scratch_pages)     # usize 溢出直接报错
  2. buffer = KvBuffer::new(…, num_blocks + scratch_pages)  # 物理页 = 逻辑 + scratch
  3. pool   = BlockPool::new(block_size, num_blocks)        # 池只认前 num_blocks 块
输出: KvCacheManager { pool, buffer }
```

于是物理缓冲被一条看不见的线切成两段:

```text
物理缓冲(一次 alloc_zeros,共 (N + S) × page_stride 个 bf16 元素)
┌────────────┬────────────┬───────┬────────────┬──────────────────────────┐
│ 页 0       │ 页 1       │  …    │ 页 N-1     │ 页 N .. 页 N+S-1         │
│ (padding)  │            │       │            │ scratch:池的事务层不可见 │
└────────────┴────────────┴───────┴────────────┴──────────────────────────┘
 └────────── 池的块 ID 空间 = 0..N ────────────┘  └── 只归调用方(hedge)──┘
```

`from_buffer` 则走反方向:缓冲已经存在(qwen35 每个模型对象自带 `kv_buffer()`),只需要配上一个新池:

```text
输入: buffer(已有), num_blocks(协商出的逻辑容量)
  1. 校验 num_blocks ≤ buffer.num_blocks()        # 逻辑不得超过物理
  2. pool = BlockPool::new(buffer.layout().page_size, num_blocks)
                                                  # 块尺寸取自缓冲几何,杜绝配错
输出: KvCacheManager { pool, buffer }
```

#### 4.2.3 源码精读

`new` 的全部实现就是委托,见 [src/manager.rs:L21-L38](https://github.com/openinfer-project/openinfer/blob/785d04871df37ddfb3e1b1432ce544b94505a801/pegainfer-kv-cache/src/manager.rs#L21-L38):`Self::new_with_scratch_pages(stream, …, num_blocks, 0)`。「无 scratch」不是独立分支,而是 scratch 为零的特例——少一条代码路径,就少一种配错的可能。

`new_with_scratch_pages` 在 [src/manager.rs:L40-L66](https://github.com/openinfer-project/openinfer/blob/785d04871df37ddfb3e1b1432ce544b94505a801/pegainfer-kv-cache/src/manager.rs#L40-L66),文档注释把 scratch 页的契约说得非常完整,值得整段读:

```rust
/// Like [`new`](Self::new), plus `scratch_pages` extra pages in the GPU
/// buffer that the pool never hands out. Their page ids are
/// `num_blocks..num_blocks + scratch_pages`; ownership and content are the
/// caller's business (e.g. the speculative hedge's alternative-chain verify
/// KV). The transaction layer is unaware of them by construction.
pub fn new_with_scratch_pages(…, num_blocks: usize, scratch_pages: usize)
    -> anyhow::Result<Self>
{
    let buffer = KvBuffer::new(
        stream, num_layers, num_kv_heads, head_dim, block_size,
        num_blocks.checked_add(scratch_pages).ok_or_else(|| {
            anyhow::anyhow!("KV pages {num_blocks} + scratch {scratch_pages} overflow")
        })?,
    )?;
    let pool = BlockPool::new(block_size, num_blocks)?;
    Ok(Self { pool, buffer })
}
```

四个要点:①scratch 页 ID 区间是**左闭右开**的 `num_blocks..num_blocks + scratch_pages`;②「所有权与内容是调用方的事务」——crate 层只保证这些页物理存在、池不发,里面写什么、怎么轮转由消费方(qwen3 hedge)自管;③「事务层按构造不可见」——池在构造时只登记了 `num_blocks` 个块(见 [src/pool.rs:L73-L79](https://github.com/openinfer-project/openinfer/blob/785d04871df37ddfb3e1b1432ce544b94505a801/pegainfer-kv-cache/src/pool.rs#L73-L79) 的 `block_count(num_blocks)`),schedule/apply/release/evict 的全部状态机都在这个命名空间里运转,ID ≥ num_blocks 的页**在池的世界里不存在**,不是「被禁止发放」而是「无法被表达」;④`checked_add` 防 `num_blocks + scratch_pages` 溢出回绕——回绕会让缓冲反而变小、scratch 区间吞掉正常页,这类静默错误必须在构造期挡下。

`from_buffer` 在 [src/manager.rs:L68-L81](https://github.com/openinfer-project/openinfer/blob/785d04871df37ddfb3e1b1432ce544b94505a801/pegainfer-kv-cache/src/manager.rs#L68-L81):

```rust
/// Pair an existing physical KV buffer with a new logical block pool.
///
/// `num_blocks` may be smaller than the physical allocation. Tensor-parallel
/// executors use this to choose the minimum common logical capacity across
/// rank-local buffers while keeping one shared page-id namespace.
pub fn from_buffer(buffer: KvBuffer, num_blocks: usize) -> anyhow::Result<Self> {
    anyhow::ensure!(
        num_blocks <= buffer.num_blocks(),
        "logical KV block count {num_blocks} exceeds physical buffer capacity {}",
        buffer.num_blocks()
    );
    let pool = BlockPool::new(buffer.layout().page_size, num_blocks)?;
    Ok(Self { pool, buffer })
}
```

### 4.3 消费方视角:TP 最小容量协商与投机 hedge 的 scratch 页

#### 4.3.1 概念说明

前两节讲的是 crate 内的机制,本节用两个真实消费方回答「这些设计为什么存在」。

**TP 与最小公共逻辑容量**:张量并行下,每个 rank 只持有 KV 头的一个分片,几何各不相同;更要紧的是,每个 rank 的物理缓冲容量是**各自按本机空闲显存画像**定出来的(qwen3 执行器在构造 `KvCacheManager` 之前先跑 `profile_kv_budget_on_worker` 得到 `budget.num_blocks`,见 [pegainfer-qwen3/src/executor.rs:L1113-L1127](https://github.com/openinfer-project/openinfer/blob/785d04871df37ddfb3e1b1432ce544b94505a801/pegainfer-qwen3/src/executor.rs#L1113-L1127))。不同 rank 显存余量不同,`num_blocks` 就可能不同。但 TP 是锁步执行:每一步算哪些请求、引用哪些块,全组必须一致——**页 ID 命名空间必须全组共享且全组等长**。于是逻辑容量只能取各 rank 的最小值,这就是 `from_buffer` 文档里「minimum common logical capacity across rank-local buffers while keeping one shared page-id namespace」的含义。

**投机 hedge 与 scratch 页**:qwen3 的 DFlash 投机解码有一条「对冲」增强——除了验证主候选链 A,再平行验证一条备选链 B。链 B 的 KV 不能直接写进该请求的正式页(会污染链 A 尚未裁决的 KV),它需要**自己的页**来写;但池的事务层不认识「临时页」这种概念。scratch 页就是解法:物理上多分配几页、逻辑上对池隐身,链 B 的页表行指向 scratch 页,输赢裁决后再决定是否整页拷回正式页。

#### 4.3.2 核心流程

qwen35 TP 的构造协商(每 rank 各自执行,结果必须一致):

```text
1. 断言所有 rank 的 page_size 一致            # 几何分片可以不同,页大小必须相同
2. min_capacity = min over ranks(本 rank kv_buffer().num_blocks())
3. kv_cache = KvCacheManager::from_buffer(first.kv_buffer().clone(), min_capacity)
4. 可用容量 = min_capacity - 1                 # 减去 padding 块
```

qwen3 hedge 每个验证步的 scratch 轮转:

```text
预备(引擎构造时):new_with_scratch_pages(…, num_blocks=N, scratch_pages=S)
  → scratch 区间 = [N, N+S),由执行器私有光标 next_scratch 管理

每一步(验证 round):
  1. scratch_end = kv_buffer.num_blocks()      # 物理上界 = N+S
     若 scratch_end == total_blocks(即 S == 0)→ 无 hedge,直接返回
  2. 为链 B 构造页表:把链 A 视图中「span 覆盖的页」替换为 scratch 页
     若 span 的第一页与已提交前缀共享(半满页):
        copy_page(orig → scratch)              # 先拷贝共享的前缀行,链 B 才能续写
  3. 链 B 在 scratch 页里写自己的验证 KV,与链 A 同批 forward
  4. 裁决:B 严格更优 → copy_page(scratch → orig) 整页拷回正式页;否则丢弃
  5. next_scratch 回卷(下一步复用同一批 scratch 页,内容覆盖即可)
```

#### 4.3.3 源码精读

TP 协商的实现在 [pegainfer-qwen35/src/tp_executor.rs:L734-L756](https://github.com/openinfer-project/openinfer/blob/785d04871df37ddfb3e1b1432ce544b94505a801/pegainfer-qwen35/src/tp_executor.rs#L734-L756):

**参考答案要点**(先自己写完再看):

1. 物理 buffer 由各 rank 按本机显存画像独立定容(qwen3 的 `profile_kv_budget_on_worker` 就是证据),显存余量不同则 `num_blocks` 不同;但 TP 锁步要求全组每一步引用同一组块 ID,页 ID 命名空间必须全组等长,故逻辑容量 = min(各 rank 物理容量),由 `from_buffer(first.kv_buffer().clone(), min_capacity_pages)` 落实。
2. 范围是 `num_blocks..num_blocks + scratch_pages`(左闭右开)。「不可能」而非「禁止」:池的底层 `BlockManager` 构造时 `block_count(num_blocks)` 只登记了 N 个块,ID ≥ N 在池的全部数据结构中不存在,schedule/apply/evict 任何路径都无法表达它们——文档所谓「The transaction layer is unaware of them by construction」。
3. `copy_page` 是物理层原语,它只知道 `Inner::num_blocks`(物理页数),**根本不持有池的引用**,「池的逻辑块数」对它是不存在的概念,因此谈不上「额外允许」或检查——`ensure!` 只对物理上界做对称校验。合法性由用途背书:hedge 的拷出(scratch→orig)与拷入(orig→scratch)两侧都可能越过逻辑边界,这正是文档注释「scratch pages past the pool's block count are valid targets」的由来。

tools.name: ScheduleWakeup
tools.description:
Schedule when to resume work in /loop dynamic mode — the user invoked /loop without an interval, asking you to self-pace iterations of a specific task.

Do NOT schedule a short-interval wakeup to poll for background work you started — when harness-tracked work finishes, you are re-invoked automatically, so polling is wasted. Instead schedule a long fallback (1200s+) so the loop survives if the work hangs or never notifies. The exception is external work the harness cannot track (a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue) — there, pick a delay matched to how fast that state actually changes.

Pass the same /loop prompt back via `prompt` each turn so the next firing repeats the task. For an autonomous /loop (no user prompt), pass the literal sentinel `<<autonomous-loop-dynamic>>` as `prompt` instead — the runtime resolves it back to the autonomous-loop instructions at fire time. (There is a similar `<<autonomous-loop>>` sentinel for CronCreate-based autonomous loops; do not confuse the two — ScheduleWakeup always uses the `-dynamic` variant.) To end the loop, call this tool with `stop: true` (omit every other field) — the loop ends immediately and no further wakeups fire.

Set `noop: true` if nothing changed — you checked and there's nothing to report ("no change", "still waiting", "quiet hold"). Set `noop: false` if something happened worth keeping — you edited a file, posted a message, advanced state, or surfaced a finding. Consecutive `noop: true` ticks are collapsed in the user's terminal view and tracked as a streak, so long quiet holds stay legible to the user without scrolling. Omit `noop` when stopping (`stop: true`).

## Picking delaySeconds

This session's requests use the default 5-minute Anthropic prompt-cache TTL. Sleeping past 300 seconds means the next wake-up reads your full conversation context uncached — slower and more expensive. So the natural breakpoints:

- **Under 5 minutes (60s–270s)**: cache stays warm. Right for actively polling external state the harness can't notify you about — a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue.
- **5 minutes to 1 hour (300s–3600s)**: pay the cache miss. Right when there's no point checking sooner — waiting on something that takes minutes to change, genuinely idle, or as the long fallback heartbeat when something else is the primary wake signal.

**Don't pick 300s.** It's the worst-of-both: you pay the cache miss without amortizing it. If you're tempted to "wait 5 minutes," either drop to 270s (stay in cache) or commit to 1200s+ (one cache miss buys a much longer wait). Don't think in round-number minutes — think in cache windows.

For idle ticks with no specific signal to watch, default to **1200s–1800s** (20–30 min). The loop checks back, you don't burn cache 12× per hour for nothing, and the user can always interrupt if they need you sooner.

Think about what you're actually waiting for, not just "how long should I sleep." If you're polling a CI run that takes ~8 minutes, sleeping 60s burns the cache 8 times before it finishes — sleep ~270s twice instead.

The runtime clamps to [60, 3600], so you don't need to clamp yourself.

## The reason field

One short sentence on what you chose and why. Goes to telemetry and is shown back to the user. "watching CI run" beats "waiting." The user reads this to understand what you're doing without having to predict your cadence in advance — make it specific.

Execute a workflow script that orchestrates multiple subagents deterministically. Workflows run in the background — this tool returns immediately with a task ID, and a <task-notification> arrives when the workflow completes. Use /workflows to watch live progress.

ONLY call this tool when the user has explicitly opted into multi-agent orchestration. Workflows can spawn dozens of agents and consume a large amount of tokens; the user must request that scale, not have it inferred. Explicit opt-in means one of:
- The user included the keyword "ultracode" in their prompt (you'll see a system-reminder confirming it).
- Ultracode is on for the session (a system-reminder confirms it) — see **Ultracode** in the workflow authoring reference.
- The user directly asked you to run a workflow or use multi-agent orchestration in their own words ("use a workflow", "run a workflow", "fan out agents", "orchestrate this with subagents"). The ask must be in the user's words — a task that would merely benefit from a workflow does not count.
- The user invoked a skill or slash command whose instructions tell you to call Workflow.
- The user asked you to run a specific named or saved workflow.

For any other task — even one that would clearly benefit from parallelism — do NOT call this tool. Use the Agent tool (if available) for individual subagents, or briefly describe what a multi-agent workflow could do and how much it would roughly cost, and ask the user whether to run it. Mention they can ask for one with "use a workflow" in a future message to skip the ask.

Every script must begin with `export const meta = {...}`: a PURE LITERAL (no variables, calls or interpolation) giving the workflow's `name`, a one-line `description` (shown in the permission dialog) and optionally `phases` — one `{ title, detail? }` per phase() call, titles matched exactly. Pass the script inline via `script` — do not Write it to a file first, and do not also set the tool's `name` input (that selects a saved workflow); it is plain JavaScript, not TypeScript.

The canonical multi-stage pattern — pipeline by default, each dimension verifies as soon as its review completes:
  export const meta = {
    name: 'review-changes',
    description: 'Review changed files across dimensions, verify each finding',
    phases: [{ title: 'Review' }, { title: 'Verify' }],
  }
  const DIMENSIONS = [{key: 'bugs', prompt: '...'}, {key: 'perf', prompt: '...'}]
  const results = await pipeline(
    DIMENSIONS,
    d => agent(d.prompt, {label: `review:${d.key}`, phase: 'Review', schema: FINDINGS_SCHEMA}),
    review => parallel(review.findings.map(f => () =>
      agent(`Adversarially verify: ${f.title}`, {label: `verify:${f.file}`, phase: 'Verify', schema: VERDICT_SCHEMA})
        .then(v => ({...f, verdict: v}))
    ))
  )
  const confirmed = results.flat().filter(Boolean).filter(f => f.verdict?.isReal)
  return { confirmed }
  // Dimension 'bugs' findings verify while dimension 'perf' is still reviewing. No wasted wall-clock.

This session has the default workflow size guideline: medium — keep workflows under 10 agents. This is a guideline, not a hard limit — follow it unless the user's prompt calls for a different scale. The user can raise or remove it with "Dynamic workflow size" in /config.
